title: Church music and how 'The Saints' was played at funerals
summary: Foster was only Catholic and says dance bands did not play hymns; Saints was slow funeral music in early days.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I was going to ask him more about that early music up in the country. Because not very many people remember much about that.
Was there much church music up there? No, we played dance music.
I mean, in singing, did you belong in the church in those days? Which church?
Catholic church, that's all. I never knew nothing but Catholic. No Catholic?
No Catholic. Yeah. I never knew nothing but Catholic.
I thought some of the other churches had a lot of singing, you know, spirituals and all that in their churches, like the Baptist.

No, you see the bands, Louis in the late days come out with playing the Saints and all that stuff. But the Saints, they played that when it was going to the funeral with a body. They played that very slow moving around, a 4-4 movement going to the funeral. They played that very early in the funeral. Yeah. See? But in the... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...

They played that very slow movement, a 4-4 movement going to the funeral. But in the later years they come out playing it in ragtime style, you know what I mean? We played places in the south, right in Texas. The man said, well we're going to play the sense. They wouldn't let you play it, you'll have to play it as a preacher, let you play it. Like, or the club was a number closer to the hymns. Just a close walk of the gym. Now we didn't play them kind of things. We didn't play nothing like that in our dance hall. We played hymns, we played them hymns, we didn't do that back in those days. And anybody will tell you that they did back in those days, they tell you something that I don't know about it. They played before me, I know the bands didn't play, they wouldn't play nothing like that. Not in our dance hall. But I played with Manuel. But I played most, a lot of the days with Manuel and Freddie and them because it was right downtown. See? Because them bands had all the work. And all your work was downtown. Yeah, in the district and all too.
